propositions: Fault-seeded testing reveals that the original burst regression test detects partial-success failures (empty JSON payload, missing record fields) that the generic property tests do not catch, establishing non-subsumption in one direction.

The generic property tests catch a sustained stall failure (F5) and list-surface emptiness (F7) that the original regression test misses, establishing non-subsumption in the opposite direction; the two oracles are complements rather than duplicates.

Reverting the actual slim-fetch-ledge fix leaves both burst tests green while only the deterministic held-lock tests fail, proving the 6-round x 4-ticket storm does not reliably detect the regression it is named for.

Standard mutation-score reduction criteria (Just et al. FSE 2014) license test removal only when it does not decrease detected faults; deletion of the original test would forfeit detection of F3 and F6 partial-success seeds, making consolidation unsafe.

The consolidation target accounts for 57.6s of CI runner cost per change (12.79–14.93s on Ubuntu, 15.34s on macOS), but that runtime is not recoverable by deletion without losing real detection power; cost recovery requires right-sizing the storm within the existing oracle rather than removing it.
